reports.note: Emergency management reported a brief tornado touched down in Fort Stockton near the intersection of Ryan and Young Streets. The tornado tracked past the Pecos County Courthouse and lifted in James Rooney Memorial Park. A NWS Survey Team found damage to metal roofs and tree branches consistent with a high-end EF-0 tornado.

Corrects previous tornado report from 3 NE Fort Stockton. Trained spotter and Pecos County EM reported a tornado NE of Fort Stockton. The tornado pulled metal wall panels from a building and overturned a small shed.
Trained spotter and Pecos County EM reported a tornado NE of Fort Stockton. Preliminary reports of damage.

tracks.note: A tornado touched down in the wooded area between Miller Creek Road and Yackin Road, rapidly moving north across Camp Jackson Road. It dissipated just east of the Camp Jackson facility, short of the Barnwell County line. Impact was primarily limited to forested areas, with high winds snapping and uprooting clusters of hardwood and softwood trees.

A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-1 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 95 mph occurred just west of Kline. The tornado developed south of Boiling Springs Rd, east of Shepherd Rd., moved to the north across a large heavily wooded field, before dissipating near Poplar Road. The tornado snapped numerous hardwood trees. This tornado was likely associated with a supercell that spawned multiple tornadoes.

A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-2 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 115 mph occurred in Barnwell. The tornado developed along Hwy 278 south of Mount Olive Cir, then continued north into the City of Barnwell, before turning northwest through Long Branch and just north of downtown Williston. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage along its path, with the most intense damage occurring in a wooded area along a field south of Freedom Road where numerous large hardwood trees were snapped and uprooted. There is also evidence that a few wooden power poles were snapped.  The tornado lifted on the north side of Williston near Wilton Drive. This tornado was likely associated with a supercell that spawned multiple tornadoes.

A tornado touched down in the swampland south of Highway 80 near rocky Creek. It moved northeast across Highway 80 and Abrams Rd, turning north and crossing Forest Hill Rd before lifting. Significant damage occurred at a residential farmstead on Hwy 80, including roof damage, multiple large trees uprooted, toppled portions of a center-pivot irrigation system, and multiple 18-wheeler trailers toppled over. The rest of the damage was mainly trees and limbs.

East Arcadia Tornado confirmed with a combination of damage and video provided by a resident north of East Arcadia. The tornado was broad and evidence suggested that it made intermittent contact with the ground, remaining mostly elevated along the path.

On Saturday, October 10th, an EF1 tornado touched down just southeast of Bethcar Church Rd. It quickly strengthened and moved northwestward, causing mostly tree damage along its path. The most significant damage was noted beginning alone Coleman Bridge Rd and continuing along Quail Run Rd where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado continued causing damage as it moved northwestward, crossing Kennedy Dr and Camp Rawls Rd with sporadic tree damage noted. The tornado likely lifted in a swampy area north of Eagerton Rd where the final snapped/uprooted trees were noted.

The tornado crossed Highway 301 west of Gravel Hill Road, causing some of the most significant damage. In total, four homes were impacted: one sustained destruction of aluminum roofing material and a front porch; another had complete roof and outer wall failure on a rear addition; and the other two sustained minor roofing damage. An outbuilding and two carports were also destroyed. The tornado then continued north through a heavily wooded area, but additional tree damage occurred just west of Moultry Loop and on Revolutionary Trail.

A weak tornado briefly touched down near Wind Mill Road, southeast of Captolo, GA, before moving north-northeast and dissipating just north of Limesink Road. Its track was periodically visible across open grass fields. Tornado damage was minor and limited to the breakage of large branches from both hardwood and softwood trees.  The  tin roof was pealed back on a standalone garage.

A rapidly intensifying tornado touched down just south of Highway 21 near Ogeechee Creek before dissipating just north of Old Poor Robin Road in far eastern Screven County, GA. The tornado produced significant tree damage along its path with numerous large hardwood and softwood trees being either snapped off or completely uprooted. One mobile home suffered major damage as a large hardwood tree fell on it. Several cars were also crushed from trees falling on them. Tree damage was observed on parts of Old Poor Robin Road, Poor Robin Road, Wiseman Road and Highway 21.

The tornado occurred at a property along Roseland Rd east of Joe Brown Hwy South. Several open farm buildings were destroyed due to roof uplift and subsequent wall failure. Debris was scattered along a narrow path. An empty grain bin was also lifted off its foundation and shifted. Sheet metal roofing was scattered along the path including high into tree canopies and into an adjacent field beyond the grove of trees.

The tornado occurred along a 3.2 mile-long discontinuous path, as it momentarily touched down and lifted several times before finally dissipating at the end of the indicated path. Damage consisted mainly of snapped and uprooted trees, large tree branches broken off, minor shingle and roof damage to several homes or structures, many fences blown over, and several power poles that were snapped and downed. There was also damage to patio furniture and signage at a service station at the intersection of Hwy 36 and Hwy 70 in Clayton.  The max wind speed was 85 mph which is an EF-0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale (EF Scale).

A brief, but strong, short-track tornado occurred on the northeast side of Candor in between Brutonville Road and I-73. Drone images and video provided by Eagle Springs Fire Chief assisted in determining the start point between Cherry Circle and Hurricane Drive where a significant number of uprooted and snapped trees occurred. The tornado quickly continued to track roughly northeast where significant damage occurred to a community center which had 3 of its exterior walls collapsed and several more softwood trees were snapped; consistent with high-end EF-1 to low-end EF-2 damage. The tornado continued across a small pond and snapped about 10 hardwood/softwood trees and removed a large portion of roof covering from a residence near Etta Drive. From this point, the tornado quickly lifted, not before snapping small branches, before reaching I-73 with no visible damage from drone footage to the northeast.

A long-track storm produced mostly EF-0 to EF-1 damage, including a short, quarter-mile stretch of EF-2 damage with maximum wind speeds estimated at 115 mph. The tornado touched down near the intersection of Skibo and Morganton roads, knocking down several trees and removing a couple of HVAC units from the Burlington Shoes store within a strip mall. The tornado then likely lifted briefly before touching down again and intensifying near the Walmart along Skibo Road, where it removed nearly 10 HVAC units from the roof, causing minor damage as they tumbled across it. The tornado continued between two hotels, where it bent and collapsed poles, damaged roofs, and rolled a car or two. As the tornado continued through the Sam’s Club parking lot, roughly a dozen cars were toppled or lifted, and one minor injury was reported. A short-lived tornado with maximum wind speeds of 105 mph initially developed along Ramsey Street near Linden, NC, and continued to track northeast. The most significant damage occurred as the tornado crossed through a residential area between Glenmont Creek Place, Hungry Creek Drive, and Rainy Beck Way. Several homes had minor roof and fence damage; however, a select few along Hungry Creek Drive sustained high-end EF-1 damage, where 50% of the windows were blown out, fence posts set in poured concrete were pulled from the ground, and wind-blown timber punctured exterior walls. The tornado continued tracking northeast into an open area, where drone photos provided by the Harnett County Deputy Fire Marshal revealed a noticeable path through a dormant cornfield and a section of downed or snapped softwood trees in a field north of Horseshoe Bend Road. A long track supercell produced an initial weak tornado near the intersection of Clito Road and Rough Rider Road in eastern Bulloch County. The National Weather Service received a witness report of a tornado on the ground and, upon conducting a ground and drone survey, found that large trees were uprooted in a convergent pattern, large branches were snapped, and a crop pivot was damaged along the path where the tornado briefly touched down in the area.

A tornado associated with the outer bands of Hurricane Isaias moved onshore near the intersection of US 98 and State Road 65 east of Eastpoint in Franklin County. The tornado was captured on video, provided by a local media outlet. The tornado moved inland approximately one mile, causing minor damage to several homes along State Road 65 and Michael Way before dissipating in a forested area.
